pages.text: A cannonball through the hull leaves a $(l)hole$(). Holes $(l)below the waterline$() let the sea in; holes above it don't, unless she sinks low enough to put them under.$(br2)Water rises in the hold, she sits lower and slows, and in the end she goes down.$(br2)Run her aground at speed and the hull is holed where she strikes.

The $(l)Galleon$()'s deep lower deck takes a lot of water, and holes in her gun deck stay dry while she rides high. But once the water is over her lower deck it pours in fast. The $(l)Brigantine$() has only one deck below, and fills quickest of all.
Patch a hole by pressing $(k:use) on it with $(item)planks$() in hand. Her supply barrels carry planks.
Bail with a $(item)bucket$() from the bucket rack: fill it from the water in the hold, then throw it over the side with $(k:use). Patch first, then bail!
